You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

use core::marker;

/// Generic peripheral accessor
pub struct Periph<PER: PeripheralSpec> {
    _marker: marker::PhantomData<PER>,
}

/// Peripheral data
pub trait PeripheralSpec {
    /// RegisterBlock associated with peripheral
    type RB;
    /// Address of the register block
    const ADDRESS: usize;
    /// Debug name
    const NAME: &'static str;
}

unsafe impl<PER: PeripheralSpec> Send for Periph<PER> {}

impl<PER: PeripheralSpec> core::fmt::Debug for Periph<PER> {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut core::fmt::Formatter) -> core::fmt::Result {
        f.debug_struct(PER::NAME).finish()
    }
}

impl<PER: PeripheralSpec> Periph<PER> {
    ///Pointer to the register block
    pub const PTR: *const PER::RB = PER::ADDRESS as *const _;

    ///Return the pointer to the register block
    #[inline(always)]
    pub const fn ptr() -> *const PER::RB {
        Self::PTR
    }

    /// Steal an instance of this peripheral
    ///
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// Ensure that the new instance of the peripheral cannot be used in a way
    /// that may race with any existing instances, for example by only
    /// accessing read-only or write-only registers, or by consuming the
    /// original peripheral and using critical sections to coordinate
    /// access between multiple new instances.
    ///
    /// Additionally, other software such as HALs may rely on only one
    /// peripheral instance existing to ensure memory safety; ensure
    /// no stolen instances are passed to such software.
    pub unsafe fn steal() -> Self {
        Self {
            _marker: marker::PhantomData,
        }
    }
}

impl<PER: PeripheralSpec> core::ops::Deref for Periph<PER> {
    type Target = PER::RB;

    #[inline(always)]
    fn deref(&self) -> &Self::Target {
        unsafe { &*Self::PTR }
    }
}

/// Raw register type (`u8`, `u16`, `u32`, ...)
pub trait RawReg:
    Copy
    + From<bool>
    + core::ops::BitOr<Output = Self>
    + core::ops::BitAnd<Output = Self>
    + core::ops::BitOrAssign
    + core::ops::BitAndAssign
    + core::ops::Not<Output = Self>
    + core::ops::Shl<u8, Output = Self>
{
    /// Mask for bits of width `WI`
    fn mask<const WI: u8>() -> Self;
    /// `0`
    const ZERO: Self;
    /// `1`
    const ONE: Self;
}

macro_rules! raw_reg {
    ($U:ty, $size:literal, $mask:ident) => {
        impl RawReg for $U {
            #[inline(always)]
            fn mask<const WI: u8>() -> Self {
                $mask::<WI>()
            }
            const ZERO: Self = 0;
            const ONE: Self = 1;
        }
        const fn $mask<const WI: u8>() -> $U {
            <$U>::MAX >> ($size - WI)
        }
        impl FieldSpec for $U {
            type Ux = $U;
        }
    };
}

raw_reg!(u16, 16, mask_u16);
raw_reg!(u32, 32, mask_u32);
raw_reg!(u64, 64, mask_u64);

    /// Raw register type (`u8`, `u16`, `u32`, ...).

import subprocess, os, shutil, sys, filecmp
ORIG="/tmp/oracle_exe"
NEW="/workspace/executable"
def run_exe(exe, args, cwd, inp=None):
    return subprocess.run([exe]+args, cwd=cwd, capture_output=True, text=True, input=inp)
def case(name, args, svd=None, inp=None):
    base=f"/tmp/cmp/{name}"
    shutil.rmtree(base, ignore_errors=True)
    results=[]
    for label,exe in [("orig",ORIG),("new",NEW)]:
        d=os.path.join(base,label); out=os.path.join(d,"out"); os.makedirs(out)
        r=run_exe(exe, args, d, inp)
        files={}
        for root,dirs,fs in os.walk(d):
            for f in fs:
                p=os.path.join(root,f); files[os.path.relpath(p,d)]=open(p,'rb').read()
        results.append((r,files))
    (r1,f1),(r2,f2)=results
    ok=True
    if r1.returncode!=r2.returncode: print(name, "RC", r1.returncode, r2.returncode); ok=False
    if r1.stdout!=r2.stdout: print(name, "STDOUT diff", r1.stdout[:500], r2.stdout[:500]); ok=False
    # stderr compare ignoring thread panic ids? print
    if r1.stderr!=r2.stderr: print(name, "STDERR diff:\n---orig\n",r1.stderr[:2000],"\n---new\n",r2.stderr[:2000]); ok=False
    if set(f1)!=set(f2): print(name, "FILES", set(f1), set(f2)); ok=False
    for k in f1:
        if k in f2 and f1[k]!=f2[k]:
            print(name, "FILE DIFF", k, len(f1[k]), len(f2[k])); ok=False
            # write diffs
            try:
                a=f1[k].decode().splitlines(); b=f2[k].decode().splitlines()
                import difflib
                diff=list(difflib.unified_diff(a,b,lineterm=''))
                print("\n".join(diff[:120]))
            except Exception as e: print(e)
    print(name, "OK" if ok else "FAIL")
    return ok
PY

fn get_cursor(src: &str) -> Cursor {
    Cursor { rest: src }
}

impl Display for LexError {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter) -> fmt::Result {
        f.write_str("cannot parse string into token stream")
    }
}

impl Display for TokenStream {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter) -> fmt::Result {
        let mut joint = false;
        for (i, tt) in self.inner.iter().enumerate() {
            if i != 0 && !joint {
                write!(f, " ")?;
            }
            joint = false;
            match tt {
                TokenTree::Group(tt) => write!(f, "{}", tt),
                TokenTree::Ident(tt) => write!(f, "{}", tt),
                TokenTree::Punct(tt) => {
                    joint = tt.spacing() == Spacing::Joint;
                    write!(f, "{}", tt)
                }
                TokenTree::Literal(tt) => write!(f, "{}", tt),
            }?;
        }

        Ok(())
    }
}

impl Debug for TokenStream {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter) -> fmt::Result {
        f.write_str("TokenStream ")?;
        f.debug_list().entries(self.clone()).finish()
    }
}

#[cfg(feature = "proc-macro")]
impl From<proc_macro::TokenStream> for TokenStream {
    fn from(inner: proc_macro::TokenStream) -> Self {
        TokenStream::from_str_unchecked(&inner.to_string())
    }

/// Marker for register/field writers which can take any value of specified width
pub struct Safe;
/// You should check that value is allowed to pass to register/field writer marked with this
pub struct Unsafe;
/// Marker for field writers are safe to write in specified inclusive range
pub struct Range<const MIN: u64, const MAX: u64>;
/// Marker for field writers are safe to write in specified inclusive range
pub struct RangeFrom<const MIN: u64>;
/// Marker for field writers are safe to write in specified inclusive range
pub struct RangeTo<const MAX: u64>;

/// Write field Proxy
pub type FieldWriter<'a, REG, const WI: u8, FI = u8, Safety = Unsafe> =
    raw::FieldWriter<'a, REG, WI, FI, Safety>;

impl<REG, const WI: u8, FI, Safety> FieldWriter<'_, REG, WI, FI, Safety>
where
    REG: Writable + RegisterSpec,
    FI: FieldSpec,
{
    /// Field width
    pub const WIDTH: u8 = WI;

    /// Field width
    #[inline(always)]
    pub const fn width(&self) -> u8 {
        WI
    }

    /// Field offset
    #[inline(always)]
    pub const fn offset(&self) -> u8 {
        self.o
    }
}

impl<'a, REG, const WI: u8, FI, Safety> FieldWriter<'a, REG, WI, FI, Safety>
where
    REG: Writable + RegisterSpec,
    FI: FieldSpec,
    REG::Ux: From<FI::Ux>,
{
    /// Writes raw bits to the field
    ///
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// Passing incorrect value can cause undefined behaviour. See reference manual
    #[inline(always)]
    pub unsafe fn bits(self, value: FI::Ux) -> &'a mut W<REG> {
        self.w.bits &= !(REG::Ux::mask::<WI>() << self.o);
        self.w.bits |= (REG::Ux::from(value) & REG::Ux::mask::<WI>()) << self.o;
        self.w
    }
}

impl<'a, REG, const WI: u8, FI> FieldWriter<'a, REG, WI, FI, Safe>
where
    REG: Writable + RegisterSpec,
    FI: FieldSpec,
    REG::Ux: From<FI::Ux>,
{
    /// Writes raw bits to the field
    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn set(self, value: FI::Ux) -> &'a mut W<REG> {
        unsafe { self.bits(value) }

pub fn render_peripheral_module(device:&Device, cfg:&Config, ctx:&Ctx, p:&PExp)->Result<String,RenderErr>{
    log::debug("svd2rust::generate::peripheral", "Checking derivation information");
    log::debug("svd2rust::generate::peripheral", "Pushing cluster & register information into output");
    log::debug("svd2rust::generate::peripheral", &format!("Pushing {} register or cluster blocks into output", p.registers.len()));
    log::debug("svd2rust::generate::peripheral", "Expanding registers or clusters into Register Block Fields");
    // find peripheral object corresponding to module: original peripheral (strip)
    let periph_obj = device.peripherals.iter().find(|per| strip_dim(&per.name)==strip_dim(&p.name_expanded) || per.name==p.orig_name).cloned().unwrap_or_else(|| device.peripherals[0].clone());
    let feat=ctx.feature_for(&p.name_expanded, p.group.as_ref());
    let mut s=String::new();
    s.push_str(&doc_attr(&p.desc)); s.push('\n');
    s.push_str(&cfg_attr_str(&feat));
    s.push_str(&format!("pub mod {} {{\n", p.own_mod));
    let path=vec![periph_obj.name.clone()];
    let block=render_block(&p.registers, device, &periph_obj, &[], ctx, "RegisterBlock", "Register block", None, false, &path)?;
    s.push_str(&block.struct_text);
    s.push_str(&block.modules_text);
    s.push_str("}\n"); Ok(s)
}

}fn vector_entries(ints:&[IntInfo], cfg:&Config, ctx:&Ctx)->(usize,String){
    let _=(cfg,ctx);
    if ints.is_empty(){ return (0,String::new()); }
    let max=ints.iter().map(|i| i.value).max().unwrap_or(0) as usize;
    let mut by_val:HashMap<u64,&IntInfo>=HashMap::new(); for i in ints{ by_val.entry(i.value).or_insert(i); }
    let mut s=String::new(); let mut prev:Option<&IntInfo>=None;
    for idx in 0..=max {
        if let Some(i)=by_val.get(&(idx as u64)){
            let emitted=emitted_features(i, prev);
            if !emitted.is_empty(){
                let feats=emitted.iter().map(|f| format!("feature = \"{}\"", crate::util::escape_rust_string(f))).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ");
                s.push_str(&format!("#[cfg(not(all({},)))]\n", feats));
                s.push_str("Vector { _reserved: 0 },\n");
                for f in &emitted { s.push_str(&cfg_attr_one(f)); }
            }
            s.push_str(&format!("Vector {{ _handler: {} }},\n", i.name));
            prev=Some(i);
        } else { s.push_str("Vector { _reserved: 0 },\n"); }
    }
    (max+1,s)
}

pub fn format_tokens(src:&str)->String{
    // Replace `Self` identifiers so syn can parse declarations like `pub enum Self`
    let mut src_owned=String::new(); { let mut last=0; let bytes=src.as_bytes(); let mut i=0; while i<bytes.len(){ if (i==0 || !(bytes[i-1].is_ascii_alphanumeric()||bytes[i-1]==b'_')) && src[i..].starts_with("Self") && (i+4>=bytes.len() || !(bytes[i+4].is_ascii_alphanumeric()||bytes[i+4]==b'_')) { src_owned.push_str(&src[last..i]); src_owned.push_str("__SVD_SELF__"); i+=4; last=i; } else { i+=1; } } src_owned.push_str(&src[last..]); }
    let src=&src_owned;
    let res= match syn::parse_file(src) {
        Ok(f) => {
            let ts=quote::ToTokens::to_token_stream(&f).to_string();

            if s.starts_with("#[") { s=format!("# [{}", &s[2..]); }

pub fn encode_html_url(url:&str, anchor:&str)->String{
    let base=url.split('#').next().unwrap_or("");
    let mut out=String::new();
    for &b in base.as_bytes(){
        let c=b as char;
        if c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || c=='\'' || matches!(c, '-'|'.'|'_'|'~'|':'|'/'|'?'|'='|'&'|';'|','|'%'|'@'|'!'|'$'|'('|')'|'*'|'+'|'['|']'){ out.push(c); } else { out.push_str(&format!("%{:02X}", b)); }
    }
    out.push('#'); out.push_str(anchor); out
}

pub fn render_block_elem_module(e:&BlockElem, device:&Device, periph:&Peripheral, ancestors:&[Props], ctx:&Ctx, path:&[String]) -> Result<String,RenderErr> {
    match e {
        BlockElem::Register(r)=>{
            // derived register
            if let Some(derived)=&r.derived_from {
                return render_derived_register(r, derived, device, periph, ancestors, ctx, path);
            }
            let eff=eff_register(device,periph,ancestors,r);
            render_register(r, &eff, device, periph, ancestors, ctx, path)
        },
        BlockElem::Cluster(c)=>{
            // Derived cluster with its own children renders as its own module (below), not an alias.
            let render_own_derived = c.derived_from.is_some() && !c.children.is_empty();
            if let Some(derived)=&c.derived_from {
                if !render_own_derived {
                let desc=c.description.as_ref().map(|x| sanitize_description(x)).unwrap_or_else(|| strip_dim(&c.name));
                let type_name=ctx.fmt("cluster", &strip_dim(&c.name), true);
                let mod_name=ctx.fmt("cluster_mod", &strip_dim(&c.name), false);
                // Locate base cluster: if path is simple and in same block, no prefix; otherwise crate path from components
                let parts:Vec<&str>=derived.split('.').collect();
                let (base_type, base_mod, prefix) = if parts.len()==1 {
                    (ctx.fmt("cluster", parts[0], true), ctx.fmt("cluster_mod", parts[0], false), String::new())
                } else {
                    // parts: peripheral, clusters..., basecluster
                    let mut pfx=format!("{}::{}", ctx.cfg.settings.crate_path.clone().unwrap_or_else(|| "crate".into()), ctx.fmt("peripheral_mod", &strip_dim(parts[0]), false));
                    for mid in &parts[1..parts.len()-1] { pfx.push_str(&format!("::{}", ctx.fmt("cluster_mod", &strip_dim(mid), false))); }
                    pfx.push_str("::");
                    (ctx.fmt("cluster", parts[parts.len()-1], true), ctx.fmt("cluster_mod", parts[parts.len()-1], false), pfx)
                };
                let mut out=String::new(); out.push_str(&doc_attr(&desc)); out.push('\n'); out.push_str(&format!("pub use {}{} as {};\npub use {}{} as {};\n", prefix, base_type, type_name, prefix, base_mod, mod_name)); return Ok(out);
                }
            }
            let desc=c.description.as_ref().map(|x| sanitize_description(x)).unwrap_or_else(|| strip_dim(&c.name));
                let type_name=ctx.fmt("cluster", &strip_dim(&c.name), true);
                let mod_name=ctx.fmt("cluster_mod", &strip_dim(&c.name), false);
                // Locate base cluster: if path is simple and in same block, no prefix; otherwise crate path from components
                let parts:Vec<&str>=derived.split('.').collect();
                let (base_type, base_mod, prefix) = if parts.len()==1 {
                    (ctx.fmt("cluster", parts[0], true), ctx.fmt("cluster_mod", parts[0], false), String::new())
